title: Pointwise representability assembles into a coherent infinity adjunction
statement: Use infinity categories, mapping spaces and coherent functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and small mapping spaces. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor; no presentability or completeness is assumed. It has a right adjoint if and only if for each $d\in\mathcal D$ the presheaf $c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(c),d)$ is representable, that is, naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,r_d)$ for some $r_d\in\mathcal C$. Dually a functor $i:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C$ has a left adjoint if and only if for each $c\in\mathcal C$ the covariant functor $e\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ is representable by an object of $\mathcal E$. The representing objects assemble to a coherent functor and an equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors; the universal representing maps are its unit or counit. The resulting adjunction has coherent units, counits and triangle identities, including their higher compatibility data.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.4.2 and its opposite; Definition 5.2.2.7 and Proposition 5.2.2.8; section 5.2.7 for fully faithful adjunctions Read online; not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text:
Necessity is the unit/counit calculation on mapping spaces, made coherent by Yoneda evaluation. Suppose $F\dashv R$, with coherent unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$. For $c\in\mathcal C$ and $d\in\mathcal D$ define $\Phi(a)=R(a)\eta_c$ and $\Psi(b)=\epsilon_dF(b)$, for $a:Fc\to d$ and $b:c\to Rd$. Naturality and the two triangle homotopies give
$$\Psi\Phi(a)\simeq a\epsilon_{Fc}F(\eta_c)\simeq a,\qquad \Phi\Psi(b)\simeq R(\epsilon_d)\eta_{Rd}b\simeq b,$$
homotopies of maps of the entire mapping spaces obtained from the given coherent transformations and triangle homotopies. Hence each $\Psi_c:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,Rd)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$ is an equivalence of spaces with homotopy inverse $\Phi_c$. To make these components one coherent transformation, apply the inverse clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] to $\mathcal E=\mathcal C$, $a=Rd$, the presheaf $P_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$ (whose action on $t$ is precomposition with $F(t)$) and the point $\epsilon_d\in P_d(Rd)$: it gives a coherent transformation $h_{Rd}\to P_d$ whose component at $c$ is $b\mapsto P_d(b)(\epsilon_d)=\epsilon_d\circ F(b)=\Psi_c(b)$. Every vertex component is an equivalence, so by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Setting $r_d=Rd$ proves representability of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(-),d)$. For the dual necessity, suppose $L\dashv i$ with unit $\eta'$ and counit $\epsilon'$. For $a:Lc\to e$ and $b:c\to i(e)$ set $\Phi'(a)=i(a)\eta'_c$ and $\Psi'(b)=\epsilon'_eL(b)$. Naturality and the triangles give
$$\Psi'\Phi'(a)\simeq a\epsilon'_{Lc}L(\eta'_c)\simeq a,\qquad \Phi'\Psi'(b)\simeq i(\epsilon'_e)\eta'_{i(e)}b\simeq b,$$
so every $\Phi'_e:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Lc,e)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ is an equivalence. The covariant clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], applied to $Q_c(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ and $\eta'_c\in Q_c(Lc)$, gives a coherent transformation $h^{Lc}\to Q_c$ with components $a\mapsto i(a)\circ\eta'_c=\Phi'_e(a)$; by the same componentwise criterion it is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)$, so $Lc$ represents $Q_c$. Coherent transformations and their parameters have the internal-functor meaning of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Necessity paragraph, expanded unit/counit computation; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1); coherence via Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) and Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK), componentwise detection of natural isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Assume the right-adjoint representability condition and fix $d$. Choose an equivalence of coherent presheaves $\theta_d:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,r_d)\simeq P_d$, where $P_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$. The Yoneda evaluation statement [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] applies because the mapping spaces are small and $\theta_d$ is coherent, not merely a collection of objectwise equivalences. Put $\epsilon_d=\theta_d(r_d)(\operatorname{id}_{r_d}):F(r_d)\to d$. The inverse formula in that statement identifies $\theta_d(c)$, on the entire mapping space and with its coherent naturality, with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d),\qquad t\longmapsto\epsilon_d\circ F(t).$$
Consequently these actual composition maps are equivalences for every $c$. No choice of maps $r_d\to r_{d'}$ has been assumed.

source.place: Sufficiency: conversion of a representing equivalence to the universal arrow, by Kerodon 03M5 and its opposite.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] to $F^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$, taking $\mathcal X=\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal Y=\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$, $x_d=r_d$ and $u_d=\epsilon_d^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its comparison map is the map of step 2 up to the canonical identifications, which are made as follows. Reversing the vertex order identifies the right-pinched space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(r_d,c)$ with the opposite of the left-pinched model of maps $c\to r_d$; this is not literally the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)$. Compare both through the arrow spaces $U$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]: since $(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^1$ with the endpoints exchanged, $U_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(r_d,c)=U_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the right-pinch inclusions $j_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},r_d,c}$ and $j_{\mathcal C,c,r_d}^{\mathrm{op}}$ are homotopy equivalences into it by that statement. Likewise for $\mathcal D$. Under these identifications $F^{\mathrm{op}}(v)\circ\epsilon_d^{\mathrm{op}}$ corresponds to $\epsilon_d\circ F(v)$, composition with a fixed edge being given by the same $2$-simplex fillers read in reverse order. A simplicial homotopy $K\times\Delta^1\to L$ reverses to $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1\to L^{\mathrm{op}}$, so a map of Kan complexes is a homotopy equivalence if and only if its opposite is. Hence the comparison maps of the criterion are equivalences because those of step 2 are. The cited criterion requires no completeness or presentability and explicitly permits nonfunctorial initial choices. It supplies a coherent left adjoint $L$ to $F^{\mathrm{op}}$; reversing every simplex of $L$, its unit and counit, and their triangle homotopies gives the coherent right adjoint $R=L^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $F$. The natural mapping-space equivalences and triangle homotopies are therefore the reversed ones supplied by the cited conclusion. In particular the counit components are universal representing maps of $P_d$; the representing objects may be taken to be $R(d)$, replacing the initial choices by equivalent representatives.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 (02FV), applied to the opposite functor.

proof.text: For dual sufficiency fix $c$ and choose a coherent equivalence $\lambda_c:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(l_c,-)\simeq Q_c$, where $Q_c(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$. The covariant clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] sends it to $u_c=\lambda_c(l_c)(\operatorname{id}_{l_c}):c\to i(l_c)$ and identifies its component at $e$ with $v\mapsto i(v)\circ u_c$. This is therefore an equivalence for every $e$, including all parameters. Now use [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] with $R=i$, $\mathcal X=\mathcal E$, $\mathcal Y=\mathcal C$, $x_c=l_c$ and this $u_c$. It supplies a coherent $L\dashv i$, natural equivalences of the two-variable mapping-space functors, and coherent unit, counit and triangle homotopies. The unit components are universal representing maps, so take $l_c=L(c)$. In both variances this is an adjunction in the coherent infinity-categorical sense delivered by the criterion: its transformations and homotopies retain their higher compatibility as coherent diagrams, rather than only as equations in the ordinary homotopy category. Together with step 1 this proves both equivalences in the statement.

Extracted universal arrows from representing equivalences using a new general infinity Yoneda evaluation statement, and reused the existing local coherent-adjoint criterion in the original and opposite variance. No Lean attachment, compiles, or live edits.
